This is the origin of `decision/gate-requires-coverage-doctest` and `decision/ci-test-gate-no-skips`. The seam's replay tests land in that suite.

This is the source of `decision/a11y-gate-breach-fails-build` and `decision/zero-flakiness`. The fake compositor must be deterministic: no `#[ignore]` for "needs a compositor", no retries, no driver of its own.

**2026-09-28-mutation-testing-to-the-epoch-boundary** — the per-chunk and CI mutation gates were removed, and the epoch-boundary audit (`run --mutants`) covers the output-discipline invariants. This matches the chunk's no-mutation-run directive. Guard holding is read by a `gate.py control`, not by a mutation gate.

**2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive** — recorded the first live reading of the takeover clause on Linux, "supplemental and never gating": a `wtype` key into a live session's window on a compositor the test started itself. This is the origin of `decision/live-readings-never-gate`, and the precedent for live compositor work. The seam's L1–L3 live-desktop measurements are recorded as fixtures and readings and never become a CI gate.

**2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola** — added the takeover clause's second live reading, on the product binary: a key the founder typed himself, with no agent typing it. It remains supplemental and never gating. This extends `decision/live-readings-never-gate`, and it is the precedent that live steps needing a human key are the founder's. The scope plans no typed key.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** — §8: `list` and `revive` each make one `claude agents --json` read (direct spawn, `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`, a 5 s kill). A failed, oversize, malformed or timed-out read fails open, and the bound falls on viola's own child, never on a key or the human. Unwrapped NAMEs print through `escape_row`. This is the direct precedent for a `hyprctl … -j` read: a capped, killed child read of untrusted output. Its time bound must join §8's list under `decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` and `decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver`.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** (a peer's refusal screened to a code word) — `reply_of`/`of_reply` screen a peer's reply with `viola_core::is_code_word` (1–64 bytes of `[a-z0-9-]`, a lower-case letter first). A non-code-word refusal reads `unknown`, and a non-code-word string detail reads nothing. This is the source of `decision/peer-replies-screened-to-code-words` and `contract/code-word/format`. The seam's closed outcome codes (ok, unsupported, unreachable, malformed) must be code words, and no compositor reply text may pass through as a detail.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** (the census of error writers and the body check) — `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` holds three guards: `error_bodies_each_name_a_writer_and_a_witness_that_stand`, `product_error_writers_are_each_named` and `thiserror_messages_interpolate_nothing`. `tests/support/events.rs` holds `assert_error_body_clean` (`absolute-path`, `caused-by`, `serde-path`, `planted`). These are the guards behind `decision/error-bodies-have-writer-and-witness` and `decision/thiserror-messages-interpolate-nothing`. A new seam error type must name its writer and witness in the census, and its `thiserror` messages must interpolate no reply text, socket path or pid.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** (`unknown`'s detail, a code word or nothing; a fault's body and the `wrapper fault` literal) — `unknown`'s detail became "a code word or nothing". Out-of-set fault codes read the fixed `wrapper fault` through `sanitised_fault`. This is the precedent for mapping untrusted upstream content to closed values. The seam's `malformed` and `unsupported` outcomes should follow the same closed-value shape.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** (the `--json` failure documents' witness) — `cli_error_documents_hold_no_path_or_upstream_text` holds each failure to one document with no path or upstream text and no ESC. This is a constraint for any later verb surfacing a seam outcome. Compositor reply text counts as upstream text and must reach no document.

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** (the client euid refusal's limit of proof) — one account can make no foreign peer and "no seam may be added". Each client seam's wiring is read only by forced refusals in remove-the-guard runs. This is a trap for the seam's guard tests: state the limit of proof the fake compositor leaves (real-socket wiring is read only live), and hold guards by `gate.py control` runs.

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** (the tui boundary and the wrapper's drop of a refused peer; hook and MCP on a refused socket directory: not-assertable) — a refused peer was added as a boundary clause that writes nothing to the outer terminal and moves no wheel. Hook/MCP seam refusals are recorded as not-assertable because they write no human-facing byte. This is the precedent for classing the Hyprland seam: it writes no human-facing byte, so it is not assertable or a boundary-only entity (cf. `decision/no-assertions-for-internal-crates` if it is a new crate). The socket-dir checks are the precedent if the request socket is chosen.

**2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary** (the tui passthrough boundary after a contained vt100 feed panic) — the boundary still holds after a contained parse panic: no viola literal (`panic`, `parse-rejected`, `unable`, `hint:`) reaches the outer terminal. This is the precedent for bounded, untrusted input never leaking to the terminal. A malformed compositor reply must be contained the same way, never as a panic.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** — the TUI passthrough boundary binds a passed `viola revive` too: it writes no line of its own while the child holds the terminal. This is the source of `contract/tui-passthrough/own-bytes`. Any seam call made while a child holds the terminal (e.g. a later `up`/console) writes nothing there.

**2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through** — the statusline start has its own zero-viola-bytes reading. `STATUSLINE_DEADLINE` (5 s, PROVISIONAL) falls on the user's own command, never on the human, and §8 lists every bound with whom it falls on. This is the precedent: a new bound (the seam's call deadline or kill) needs its §8 line naming its bearer.

**2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id** — the first §8 time bound, the dialog deadline, bounds the driver and never the human. This is the start of the register behind `decision/time-bounds-never-on-human`, which the seam's deadlines extend.

**2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint** — the send readiness gate's `GATE_MAX_WAIT` falls on the driver only. A human key during the wait wins, and its case is sequenced on records, never a timer. This is part of the time-bounds register. It is also the sequencing precedent: seam tests should wait on records or deadlines, not sleeps, to stay flake-free.
**2026-10-10-budget-governor** — the budget pause was added to §8 as a driver-only bound. It is in the time-bounds register (`decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver`) that a seam bound extends.
**2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** — the MCP `wait` cap (`WAIT_CAP` 50 000 ms) was added as a driver-only bound. It is in the time-bounds register.

**2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row** — the confirm windows (`CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` 10 s, `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` 40 s) were added as driver-only bounds. They are in the time-bounds register.

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** (the dialog hold bounds owned by 0.2.0's first entry) — `DIALOG_HOLD_MIN`/`DIALOG_HOLD_MAX` stay PROVISIONAL, owned by "0.2.0's first entry". Check whether this Epoch 1 — Foundation chunk is that owner. If it is not, leave the bounds alone.

Builds viola's own Hyprland seam: the one place the binary talks to the compositor, carrying only the relied-on window queries and dispatches the later window entries need, no general Hyprland client.
Each compositor reply is read capped, treated as untrusted upstream output, parsed tolerantly into closed viola types, and every seam call ends in a closed outcome code logged codes-only.
Outside Hyprland the seam answers a closed unsupported outcome; a fake compositor replays scrubbed, live-recorded replies so the seam's tests run green in CI where no compositor runs.
Measures the relied-on reply shapes and effects live once each as named operator steps (read-only queries; dispatches that focus or move a window or show a workspace), which record the fixtures the fake replays.
Builds no verb and adds no CLI output: open, focus, up, adopt and the fleet console are their own entries.

A new internal component, the compositor seam: the sole place any Hyprland request, reply shape or socket is named, as the pty and channel seams are for their crates; it prints nothing of its own to any terminal.

Compositor replies are untrusted peer output: read under a frame cap and refused past it, parsed into closed types; window titles, classes and all other reply text are content, never a command, and reach no log line, error or refusal — the reply is screened down to closed outcome code words.

Codes-only diagnostics: each seam call emits one closed outcome code (ok, unsupported, unreachable, malformed, ...) through the observability event macro, carrying no reply text, window address, pid, path or socket name; these diagnostics go to the log, never to the terminal.
The seam's error types and messages interpolate nothing taken from a reply or the environment; a failure surfaces only as its closed outcome code.
State: no compositor reachable — the seam returns a closed unsupported outcome, never a panic and never a guess.
Linux only; window features target Hyprland only; CI stays on ubuntu-latest.
The fake compositor replay: the seam's tests replay recorded replies on ubuntu-latest and must run green there — no test skipped or gated on a live compositor being present.

Live measurement is operator-only: the named live-desktop steps record facts and fixtures but never gate CI; the lock state is read first before any dispatch and the run stops on locked, never unlocking.
Recorded replies are fixtures scrubbed like every fixture: no addresses, paths, socket names or other host detail carried into the repository.
Every test or control that spawns viola run, mcp, a wrapper or a compositor client carries a kill deadline; time bounds fall on the test driver, never on a human.

No mutation run, local or dispatched; a guard test's one-off control runs through the gate's control step under a kill deadline, holding only when the control's own case ran and failed with the guard removed.
No verb is built: the chunk adds no CLI verb, help row, refusal, exit code or --json document, and claims no capability whose acceptance needs a verb.
A red or defect found here folds into the chunk as an inferred item with its own acceptance; one found outside the scope is carried forward to its owner entry.

body_fields.convention: each new test runs inside the existing nextest suites, its failure a nextest failure, with no separate a11y driver or suite
the CI test gate allows no skipped test
each new test is deterministic — zero flakiness, no retries, a breach fails the build
each new log line stays off the terminal; run diagnostics never reach it
each new error type's messages interpolate nothing; peer replies are screened to code words

body: Colour and SGR rows — amber, bold, dim, NAME truncation, colour decision inputs, word beside every SGR span: the seam prints nothing styled.
The CLI verb output contracts — help rows, list board and captions, revive, link and unlink, verify, wait, send, plugin install: no verb is built here.
Screen-reader targets and setups (Orca with GNOME Terminal or with foot on Hyprland): manual passes over the CLI and TUI, not over the compositor seam.
Human keystroke, wheel, focus/mouse/resize and vt100 feed panic rows of the TUI passthrough: the seam does not sit on the outer PTY.
Keyboard navigation of the fleet console: that belongs to the fleet a11y verification entry, not this seam.
Browser, web, touch, contrast, focus-management, WCAG mapping and structured violation JSON rows: viola has no graphical frontend.
Budget gate, dialog hold, config.json values and MCP tool contracts: the seam neither sends nor answers dialogs nor serves MCP.

Builds viola's own Hyprland seam: the one place the binary talks to the compositor, carrying only the relied-on window queries and dispatches the later window verbs need, no general Hyprland client.
Each compositor reply is read capped at the frame cap and refused past it, parsed tolerantly into closed viola types as untrusted upstream output, and every seam call ends in a closed outcome code logged codes-only.
Outside Hyprland, with no compositor reachable, the seam answers a closed unsupported outcome, never a panic and never a guess.
A fake compositor replays replies recorded live on the founder's host and scrubbed like every fixture, so the seam's tests run green on the one ubuntu-latest CI leg where no compositor runs.
No verb is built and no capability is claimed: open, focus, up, adopt and the fleet console stay their own entries.

The new Hyprland seam as a product seam: the single component that names a Hyprland request, reply shape or socket, as the pty and channel seams are the single users of their crates; nothing outside it reaches the compositor, and tests reach it only through that seam.

The relied-on request set only: window queries for clients (window address, pid, workspace, position and size), the active window, workspaces and the active workspace, and monitors; dispatches that focus a window, show a workspace and place a window.
The bounded reader of each compositor reply: read through take(MAX_FRAME + 1) and refused past the frame cap, the same cap every other external reader keeps.

The tolerant reply parser: reply text is untrusted upstream output parsed into closed viola types, missing and unknown fields tolerated, never a panic on malformed input; as a new parser surface it owes property and fuzz-style coverage of its invariants.

Reply content never escapes: window titles, classes and every other reply text are content, never a command, and reach no log line, error message, error body or refusal; error types interpolate nothing from the reply.

Codes-only logging of the seam: each seam call ends in a closed outcome code (ok, unsupported, unreachable, malformed and the like) emitted through obs_event! as a structured JSON process log line, carrying no reply text, window address, pid, path or socket name.
The closed unsupported outcome outside Hyprland: when no compositor is reachable the seam returns unsupported, never panics, never guesses; the process keeps the zero-panic rule.

The fake compositor: a test double replaying recorded replies so the seam's tests run on ubuntu-latest without a compositor; it is a real stub process or listener standing in for an external process, held byte for byte to the recordings it replays, never to hand-written replies.

The recorded compositor fixtures: replies recorded live on the founder's host, scrubbed of home paths, usernames and real data like every fixture, walked by the fixture hygiene check, and kept per recorded Hyprland version, the version read with each recording, in a record parallel to the Claude capability ledger.

Live measurement is no test layer: the live compositor reads (read-only queries, focus and workspace dispatches with the locked state read first and a stop on locked, never an unlock) are named operator steps outside CI; CI never touches a real compositor, as it never touches the real agent CLI.

The transport's spawn and socket rules: a compositor client resolved on PATH is spawned directly, with no shell and an absolute path, as viola run resolves its child; a request socket under the runtime directory would owe the same owner-only 0700 and owner checks as the channel's socket directory, refused and never repaired, or a recorded reason it does not.

The new environment read of the Hyprland instance signature: a new environment read needs its own Decisions Log entry; tests feed it per child process and never mutate the test process's own environment.

The seam's placement as a new sync workspace member or a module of the root binary: either way it builds without tokio, is wired into the module tree with no orphan module, and, as a new crate, takes its row in the crate table and its deny bans with their probes.

Every test or control that spawns viola run, mcp, a wrapper or a compositor client carries a kill deadline and is held by a drop guard; waits key on logged events and outcomes, never on sleeps or retries.

A guard's proof without a mutation run: no mutation run, local or dispatched, in this chunk; a guard test's one-off control is a bounded remove-the-guard witness under a kill deadline, holding only when the control's own case ran and failed with the guard removed.
Linux alone: the window features are Hyprland only, tests run on Linux, and CI stays the single ubuntu-latest leg.

body_fields.convention: Each new test function is named by the test-naming rule, written as an inline unit test or a table-driven rstest case where it fits, and run by nextest.
Each new test creates its own private home and directories through tempfile and shares no mutable state with tests running in parallel.
Each new fixture is synthetic or scrubbed, recorded rather than hand-written, and passes the fixture hygiene walk, its hits reported by class only.
Each new log line is one structured JSON line with the process log line fields, codes-only, with any detail kept apart.
Each new test avoids the anti-patterns: no sleeps, no retries, no Debug-string comparison, literal oracles, no real network, no mocking of what viola does not own, no ignore parking.
Each new module and test counts toward the workspace coverage floor with no new exclusion, and any test failure fails the build.
